acceptedVulnerabilities: None. No vulnerabilities were accepted during the reporting period, and no POA&M items are open.
certificationDataChanges: A-LIGN's initial Ongoing Certification Report for A-SCEND. For baseline context, identity and platform changes between initial certification (2025-09-17) and the start of this period included: a self-hosted identity broker (Verity) for federal users with SAML and OIDC federation through ORY Polis / BoxyHQ Jackson (see Transformative Changes), the Go FIPS 140-3 cryptographic module enabled in the broker, hardened distroless container images with STIG scanning, SBOM generation, and Binary Authorization on Cloud Run, the API gateway replaced with Envoy, authentication cookies set Secure and SameSite, and a system use notification (AC-8) on the federal sign-in pages.

Baseline context, continued: before this period, product analytics events and outbound notification emails were suppressed for federal users; AI-assisted features (in-product assistant, AI citations, batch generation of AI reports) were extended and remain controlled per account by feature flags; optional integrations with commercial GRC and CRM platforms (HITRUST MyCSF, Vanta, MuleSoft) were approved for commercial tenants only; and the authorization boundary, network architecture, and data flow diagrams were rebuilt to show Cloudflare for Government in-boundary as the WAF and sole network ingress.

Published a machine-readable Certification Package Overview (2026-09-01) in the public FedRAMPx20 repository. It lists leveraged FedRAMP services (Google Cloud FR1805751477, Microsoft 365 GCC, Cloudflare for Government FR2000863987A) and non-certified workforce identity providers.

Session security strengthened: sign-out now revokes the token pair server-side, revoked refresh tokens are rejected (fail closed), sign-out returns users through the identity provider they signed in with, and cross-site request forgery protection was extended to the sign-in discovery flow.

AI-assisted features: automatic AI testing-note generation is gated by an account-level feature flag, and AI analysis results now record their provenance (model foundation, prompt version, and whether content was auto-generated).

Infrastructure hardening: DNSSEC validation for VPC DNS, a TLS 1.2 minimum on gateway-to-service connections, a FIPS build of the Cloudflare tunnel connector, Binary Authorization extended with least-privilege build service accounts, a browser error-reporting proxy restricted to internal ingress, and a strengthened database audit logging (pgaudit) configuration.
Commercial GRC integrations gained regional support (Vanta multi-region; Drata EU and APAC endpoints). Commercial third-party integrations are not enabled for federal tenants.

changes: Update the public Secure Configuration Guide and Certification Package Overview to describe federal SSO through the Verity identity broker, replacing the current Auth0 setup instructions.

Publish the next Ongoing Certification Report on January 15, 2027, covering October 16, 2026 through January 15, 2027, and hold a Quarterly Review within 3 to 10 business days after each report is published.
Simplify federal SSO onboarding with SSO setup invitation emails and account discovery by email or account name at sign-in.
Launch a partner portal and partner API backed by a dedicated fine-grained authorization service (OpenFGA). Boundary applicability will be determined before any federal data is in scope.
Commercial third-party integrations will not be enabled for federal tenants without prior interconnection review and significant change notification.

transformativeChanges: Federal identity and authentication: replaced the commercial third-party identity service (Auth0) for federal users with a self-hosted identity broker inside the authorization boundary. Verity brokers SAML and OIDC federation through ORY Polis / BoxyHQ Jackson, signs tokens with Cloud KMS keys, and supports server-side token revocation. Accounts are designated as federal through an administrative setting, and A-SCEND then automatically refuses access to those accounts from any session that did not sign in through agency SSO. Polis federation was added in June 2026 and enforced for federal accounts with Release 26.7 on 2026-07-07, shortly before this period; it is reported here because this is A-LIGN's initial Ongoing Certification Report. Auth0 remains in use only for commercial users and handles no federal data.
updatedRecommendations: Federal agencies must connect A-SCEND to their agency identity provider (SAML or OIDC) through the federal SSO setup flow, and that IdP should enforce phishing-resistant MFA (KSI-IAM-01). Federal accounts are required to sign in through agency SSO.
Do not connect commercial third-party integrations (for example Vanta or HITRUST MyCSF) to accounts or projects that contain federal data. These integrations are not enabled for federal tenants.
Users should sign out explicitly at the end of a session. Sign-out now revokes the session server-side.
